question: Under correct post-fix truth, what magnitude threshold reliably identifies PAB-aligned (spec) bright epochs, and how rare are +/-X spec anchors cohort-wide?
hypothesis: The buggy-era bright_threshold=11 is too loose under correct truth; a calibrated post-fix threshold gives higher PAB-alignment purity.
narrative_md: The buggy-era bright_threshold=11 is too loose under correct truth: at mag<11 only 22% of 'bright' epochs are within 5° of PAB. Calibrated post-fix threshold is mag<8 (P(<5°)=0.60, rising to 1.00 at mag<6). The m096 '87% of seeds lack +/-X spec constraints' claim softens to 56/100 under correct truth — still a majority, so +/-X-anchor architectures are limited to ≤44/100 seeds. 19/100 seeds have zero bright peaks. Cached min_ang_dist fields make this a 0.6 s cohort calibration with no rendering.
